status: LIVE design data v4: the vertical slice (milestones M1, M2a and M2b; survival_gdd.md version 4). The game and tests/survival/test_survival_data.gd read these rows. Every number is tunable.
summary: Barter first, coin and credit optional: the reference value (rv) every trade and test measures in, the barter valuation (need, scarcity, season, relationship) and the trade window's rules, goods, the slice's markets and partners, services (labour, lessons, loans), the firewood wage (coin or rations), the income ladder in rv, and the optional credit year.
id_rules: Ids are stable strings (prefix.name). Never rename an id once saves exist; add an alias instead. Display names are separate and may change. An id is defined in exactly one place: the live file or the backlog.

milestones.M1: A winter night: fire, shelter, cold, hunger, sleep, time safety; the fort region only; one background; 1765
milestones.M2a: A winter from the woods: living from the manor woods through the winter by your own hands (gathering, hides, sewing, snares, snowshoes, a half-faced camp, a hung cache, ice fishing); plain barter with the sutler, the trader, the garrison's soldiers, a farm family from German Flatts and an old hunter; credit and the fall outfit as options; the second background
milestones.M2b: Learning from neighbours: lessons, watching, examining, quality standards, haggling, promises and loans
milestones.M3: The year turns: the full almanac, seasons and weather content, the summer goal (bark and a cabin), fishing, frogs, ginseng, one played wage job; the fur cap and robe, leggings, carving, casting balls, the cache pit, char cloth and spruce beer
milestones.M4: People: NPC schedules and tiers at the fort, standing, invitations, the soldiers and the lieutenant as mentors; Native characters only after the relevant nation's sign-off
milestones.M5: The map: the Carry, the valley, the town and the hunting grounds, travel and camps, other markets and backgrounds
milestones.post: After M5 and not yet planned: the 1757 and 1761 starts and their eras, detailed illnesses, thirst, potash, upstream canoe and bateau travel, the Proxy NPC tier, languages beyond English, French, Mohawk and Oneida

source_keys.A: Bundled animation clip names and asset IDs
source_keys.N: graph_analysis/survival/survival_gdd.md, sources list (N:3 = source N3; N33 onward added in version 3)

basis_keys.S: sourced: checked against a primary source, a scholarly work or an institutional page; web summaries and popular pages do not qualify
basis_keys.H: standard historiography (books in the GDD sources list); verify before quoting
basis_keys.H-regional: true for one region's trade or society (named in the row); not yet checked for New York
basis_keys.M: modern science or medicine sets the mechanic (period explanation may differ)
basis_keys.D: design value for balance, or a figure resting on web summaries; not a checked historical record

currency.account: whole pence in New York currency, shown as pounds, shillings and pence
currency.from_region: Each region's institutions (map_regions.json institutions) name its currency; the account and display use New York currency in the New York frame.

pennsylvania.name: Pennsylvania currency
pennsylvania.note: 7 s 6 d to the dollar (Ohio node)

livre.name: livres (French)
livre.note: display only for French goods; approximate [D]

currency.convert: new_york_d = amount_d * 96 / currency.d_per_dollar (every wage and price records its source currency)
currency.chain: 1 beaver (a good prime skin, the unit the 1761 post tariffs counted in) = 1.5 bucks = 144 d New York (12 s); anchored to Albany's 1766 beaver price (an 88 lb pack settled 33 pounds 7 s 4 d, N:3) and the 1761 Detroit stroud tariff (2 beaver or 3 buckskins, E:S14)

barter_display.north: beaver (a prime skin), with 'lb of beaver' on the trader's weigh sheet as Albany sold it by the pound

currency.wampum: Not an inventory item and not a currency in the game: councils exchange wampum as a record and pledge in NPC diplomacy only. Historically wampum was still a manufactured commodity in the 1760s that traders and the Indian Department bought in bulk for diplomacy (N:38); keeping it out of the player's inventory is a design choice, not a claim that it was never traded.

price_layers.rule: Every good has two layers. cash_retail_d is the cash price in the valley and at Schenectady; the sutler adds her carriage markup. barter.beaver is the trader's tariff value in beaver. The gap between the two is the trader's overplus (tested within 1.2-2.2 for imports).
price_layers.overplus_note: For trade goods the barter value over cash retail sits between 1.2 and 2.2: the margin that paid for carriage, risk, credit and the trader's living.
price_layers.to_replace: Rows tagged D are placeholders until checked against the Johnson Papers tariffs (1761, 1765), the Fort Pitt trading post papers (1757-65), the Baynton, Wharton and Morgan invoices, the Albany ledgers (Roseboom) and store accounts.

settlement.rule: How the trader pays and how books carry (review 2 of v2, the ladder issue). Income anywhere in the design is compared in cash-equivalent pence.
trader_pays_in: goods at the barter tariff (his price list in beaver)
book credit at the barter value, carried on his book between visits and usable at any later visit or against the outfit debt
coin at coin_rate x the barter value (cash was scarce up the valley and he discounts it)
settlement.cash_equivalent: cash-equivalent pence = barter value x coin_rate; coin_rate is set near 1 / the typical basket's overplus (tested within 0.05), so taking goods and taking coin come out about even
settlement.barter_pays_cash_debt: only by taking coin at coin_rate and paying it over (the sutler keeps a cash tally)
settlement.sutler_buys_pelts: for coin at pelt_cash_mult (0.6) x the good's cash value, any day: less than the trader, but now
settlement.book_account: Each creditor keeps one account per player: charges, credits and payments by date; the ledger shows every account, its balance and its due event.
settlement.no_spread_on_barter: At the barter tariff the trader's margin is the overplus: pelts are credited at tariff value (x prime, grade, condition) with no further spread.

pricing.cash_buy: round(cash_retail_d * market.markup * season(profile, month) * scarcity * (1 + spread_eff))
pricing.cash_sell_pelts: cash_retail_d * pelt_cash_mult * prime * grade * condition (coin, any day)
pricing.barter_sell: barter.beaver * beaver_d * prime * grade * condition (credited in goods, book or coin at coin_rate)
pricing.spread_eff: clamp(market.spread - 0.10 * trade/100 - 0.0005 * standing, 0.10, 0.6) x trade_price_mult (drink worsens it)
pricing.stock_caps: each market holds at most its stock target; the sutler restocks every 3 game days in open season (every 6 in deep snow); the trader brings only what his visit carries
pricing.trade_bonus: the trader rounds a known hunter's furs up: +0.08 x Trade/100 on barter sales (not counted in the balance reference)
pricing.pelt_value: items.json pelt_rules multiply the value before the market terms

a felling axe, about 6 s New York
a trade gun or fusil, about 40 s New York [D]
about 3 s 6 d New York the lb on the frontier (N:26)
about 8 s; scarce at the trader (stock cap 4, to revisit after verification, N:36)
one buck: the 1761 Detroit tariff counted 3 buckskins to 2 beaver (E:S14)
the garrison meat channel pays its own price
valley retail; the sutler adds carriage
about 1 s 6 d a quart ready money (N:25)

markets.name: The sutler's store
markets.rum_note: The commandant licenses the sutler and regulates her rum; no drinking spectacle.
markets.restock: a bateau or sleigh from Schenectady every 3 game days in open season; every 6 in deep snow

meat_channel.rule: The garrison's one fresh-meat channel: the sutler buys for the mess at one price, with its own cap for fresh meat and for jerky, times the era's army-demand multiplier (a peace detachment buys a third). There is no separate garrison-meat job and no second price (review 2 of v2, the hunting issue).

buys.pelt_rule: Furs and skins for coin at 0.6 of their cash value, any day: the fallback between the trader's visits.

credit.who: people known to the garrison (garrison standing >= 10)
credit.interest_note: simple interest on an overdue store tally, below New York's legal ceiling of 7% (1737 act, N:37)
credit.variant_note: The balance report's R3: the 'On the sutler's tally' start raises her limit to 360 d so the tally is not closed from the first day.

markets.sells_months_note: The river closes and she sells out of winter clothing by November; from March she stocks it again (the arbitrage guard's stock-out rule, redesign_economy.md 6.2).

markets.name: The Schenectady trader (visits)
markets.stock_note: The steel-trap cap of 4 is a design value to revisit once the tariffs and ledgers are checked (N:36); a paid-in-full settlement raises it to 8 for that hunter.
markets.settlement: economy.json settlement (goods, book credit, or coin at 0.6)

credit.who: hunters the trader knows or is introduced to
credit.interest_note: no interest on an outfit account: the margin is in the overplus [H]

markets.note: In 1765 a Schenectady merchant's man coming up with the boats and, in winter, by sleigh. At M5 the same trader keeps the store at the Carry (backlog mkt.post_trader).
markets.barter: npcs.json trade_behaviours.tb.post_tariff (his tariff is his valuation)

markets.name: The soldiers of the detachment (evenings)
markets.restock: their issue: once a game month
markets.note: Two soldiers of the detachment trade from their issue in the evenings at the sutler's store: winter clothing while the sutler has none, fresh meat, a hand at the woodpile.

markets.name: The farm family from German Flatts (market days)
markets.note: German Palatine farms at German Flatts, about 15 miles down the valley; garrisons bought fresh food locally (E:S58). Four market days, the last with the militia muster [H/D: verify the visits and goods].

services.unit: game night in the sutler's loft
game hour of a named job for the other party
services.fulfil: worked off by the due date at the job's place (livelihoods.json jobs[].where) (SurvivalTrade.work_off); kept labour adds standing (labour_given), trust and Trade experience

services.unit: a tool lent for N game days
services.fulfil: returned by the due date or its rv is owed

services.unit: a day's meals and a place by the fire for 4 game hours of work (working for one's keep)
services.rule: the labour line (7 d of rv a game hour) buys food at the partner's terms: 4 game hours buy about three meals of cornmeal from the sutler in any month; never coin. A no-money safety net for a newcomer (redesign_balance_report.md F3) [D; H: verify the custom and its terms]. It is a trade of work for board, not hospitality, which in this design is a gift that cannot be farmed.

wages_rule.rule: A game day's wage stands for five historical days' pay, the same factor that sets food and trap nights. Wage work is played. Openings are limited by season.

ladder.unit: cash-equivalent pence per game day (economy.json settlement)
ladder.text: Every safe wage is at most half of skilled trapping's cash-equivalent income (skilled trapping at least twice the best safe wage), and novice trapping and hunting are at least 0.8 of a common day wage (72 d).
ladder.rv_rule: Restated in rv (redesign_economy.md 9.5): the rules stay (skilled trapping at least twice the best safe wage; novice work at least 0.8 of a common wage) and a subsistence line is added: the rv of food, clothing and stores made and kept per game day (liv.living_from_the_woods, 60-110 rv).

wages_rule.capital_rule: Capital wages (horses, wagons) are backlog; the backlog check tests payback of at least one season after explicit loss rates and daily income of at most twice skilled risky income.

wages.hist: cutting and stacking cordwood by the cord, about 1 s 6 d New York a cord [D; verify against garrison firewood contracts]; a good axeman cut about a cord a day, five cords a game day at the flow factor
wages.openings: the garrison's winter need, 40 cords from Early October to Late March (about 10 game days of work)
wages.rule: cords per game day rise with Woodcraft (4 at 0, 5 at 50 or more)
wages.rations_note: 4 lb of flour and 1.5 lb of salt pork a cord, about the coin's worth in rv (27 d against 18 d coin: coin was scarce and rations were the garrison's own stores) [D; verify against garrison contracts]

army_demand.rule: Peace garrisons buy about a third as much as in war; the meat channel's caps carry the multiplier per era.

credit.rule: Optional. The fall outfit on the trader's book is one way to start the year, never the only one (GDD section 11.9). Books are credit obligations graded at the spring settlement; the settlement grades only accounts with a balance or an outfit charged.
credit.first_outfit: backgrounds.json credit.first_outfit_limit_barter_d (hunter 1,100; provincial 1,000), taken with trade.take_credit at the fall credit by anyone who chooses; the 'Outfitted on credit' start variant adds a carried book (backgrounds.json start_variants)
credit.sizing_rule: A first outfit is 40-60% of a novice trapper's season net (tested) for players who take one.
credit.next_limit: clamp(0.5 x the barter value of furs and skins the player sold to this trader over the season, 800, 3000) x the grade multiplier
credit.payments: at every visit (fall credit, the winter visits, the settlement), in furs, book credit or coin

unlocks: the trader's steel-trap cap for you rises from 4 to 8

part_paid.rest: rolls over on the book, no interest

unpaid.when: less than half paid by the end of the window

credit.warning: The almanac and the debt icon warn from Mid March, only while an account is open.

interest.note: Zero on the trader's outfit book (the margin is in the overplus, H); simple interest on an overdue store tally at the sutler (and, in the backlog, the valley store and the Albany merchant), under New York's 7% ceiling of 1737 (N:37).

credit.persistence: Debt persists and follows the player: the sutler and the trader correspond within a game day.

collection.settler: the creditor takes up to half the value of your next fur sale
collection.woodsman: the creditor takes the whole of your next fur sale until the debt is met
collection.hard_winter: after 3 game days late the creditor's man seizes carried furs and goods

credit.debt_clock: The ledger shows each account, balance and due event; the HUD shows a debt icon from 3 game days before a window opens and while any debt is overdue.
credit.grading_applies_to: accounts with a balance or an outfit charged; a player with no book sees the spring visit as a market

aliases.currency.units.made_beaver_d: beaver_d (v3): the made beaver was the Hudson's Bay Company's unit
aliases.job.garrison_meat: merged into the sutler's meat channel (v3)

reference_value.rule: rv = cash_retail_d (the valley cash price already on every good). Everything made, kept, bartered or sold is measured in rv by the authority and the tests. Players see cues, not pence, unless their Trade tier or the ledger toggle shows numbers (barter.cues). Cash-equivalent pence (barter x the coin rate) stay only where coin actually changes hands at the trader.

services.labour_note: the common wage of 72 d a game day over about 10 working hours

barter.rule: Goods for goods (and coin, labour, lessons, loans and promises) in one trade window between two parties (an NPC or, later, a player). An NPC accepts when what it gets is worth at least what it gives times its terms; values come from need (the wants tier, stepping down as its quota is met), scarcity (the keeps tier, market stock and the local cap), season (which tier a good sits in each month) and relationship (standing tier, trust and Trade), never from a fixed price list. There is no special rule for food.
barter.value_in: rv x min(W, local cap) x Q, clamped to value_in_clamp x rv; the trader's is his tariff
barter.value_out: rv x K x markup (the sutler: her cash price before the spread; the trader: his tariff), clamped to value_out_clamp x rv
barter.accept: sum value_in(offered) >= sum value_out(asked) x (1 + margin + tier_adj - discount x Trade/100) x drink

local_cap.rule: a want for a good some other partner present that day offers is at most mult x that partner's base price (rv x K x markup; the trader's tariff)

barter.terms_floor_rule: No partner's terms fall below 0.90, whatever the standing, Trade and haggling: with the local cap at 0.7, a same-day round trip between two partners returns at most 0.7 / (0.9 x 0.9) = 0.86 of the price paid (T11). Added 2026-09 when the v4 gate test found a 1.24 round trip (cornmeal from the farm family to the old hunter at Trade 100, trusted, fully haggled).
barter.quota_rule: a want steps down one tier each time its quota is met within the partner's period: one visit for a visiting partner, one game month for a resident one
barter.coin: an NPC counts coin received at 1 d a penny and asks coin_premium x value when paying coin out (coin was scarce up the valley)

haggle.rule: the partner opens at (1 + margin + 0.10) and its floor is (1 + margin + tier_adj - the Trade discount); a press moves the ask toward the floor; a failure costs patience; at 0 patience the window closes for the game day

deal_text.short: they will not take it as it stands
deal_text.generous: they are doing well by it: you are giving more than they ask

cues.rule: the window shows cues with a reason by default; a five-step bar from Apprentice Trade; the wants table from Journeyman; numbers (each line's value to the partner, and the floor) from Adept or with the ledger toggle, which never shows an NPC's floor below Adept

commit.rule: the authority re-checks presence, that no party is dead, asleep, senseless or in combat, every stack and quantity, tradeability and carry; then applies every removal and addition in one step, writes obligations and the item ledger, and emits trade_committed; a repeated commit of the same session and version never applies twice

barter.wampum: never an inventory item or medium: a design choice (currency.wampum)
